::: {#def-separability .theorem}
## Separability

An [exposure mapping](#def-exposure-mapping) $g_i$ is separable if it can be written as unit $i$'s own value of each covariate, alongside one summary per covariate:

$$
g_i(\mathbf{X}_1,\dots,\mathbf{X}_K) = \Big[ \underbrace{\begin{pmatrix} X_{1i} \\ \vdots \\ X_{Ki} \end{pmatrix}}_{\in\, \mathbb R^{K}},\, \underbrace{g_{1i}(\mathbf{X}_1),\, \dots,\, g_{Ki}(\mathbf{X}_K)}_{\text{each} \,\in\, \mathbb R}\Big]^T,
$$

where $X_{ki} \in \mathscr O_i$ is unit $i$'s own entry of covariate $\mathbf X_k$, and each $g_{ti} : \{0,1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, called a **component function** of $g_i$, summarizes covariate $\mathbf X_t$ over the other units. A structural equation is separable if its exposure mapping is.
:::
